name: prompt-lab
desc: Free, open-source prompt testing bench for local models on Windows — variables, version diffs, batch runs. 100 MB portable, offline, MIT.
features: ✅ **Variable slots** — write prompts with {{topic}} and {{tone}} placeholders, then run a matrix of test values
✅ **Version diff** — every edit saved as a revision; side-by-side diff shows what actually changed
✅ **Batch matrix runs** — variables crossed with models, outputs collected in one result grid
✅ **Side-by-side outputs** — old prompt versus new prompt on the same inputs, scored with quick labels
✅ **Case import** — CSV and JSON test cases pulled in without retyping prompts
✅ **Run history** — every run timestamped with model, settings and full output, searchable
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and inference backend bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Feature | **prompt-lab** | Open WebUI | LM Studio | PromptPerfect |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Free | Paid |
| Variable matrix runs | **Yes** | No | No | Partial |
| Prompt version diff | **Yes** | No | No | Partial
| Batch CSV test cases | **Yes** | No | No | Yes web
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Docker | Installer | Browser
faqQ: how to test and improve prompts for local LLMs without guesswork?
faqA: Editing a prompt and eyeballing one answer proves nothing; real improvement needs the same inputs run against old and new versions. prompt-lab keeps a diffed history, runs variable matrices in batch and stores every result row. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline, no account.
s1: Dark lab (#121418, teal #2DD4BF): template editor left with {{topic}} highlighted, variable value matrix center, result grid right with model columns and score chips.
s2: Version diff view: two prompt revisions in split panes, changed lines tinted, restore button on the older revision, run-count badge reading tested 7 times.
s3: Batch runner: 3 variables by 2 models grid at 83 percent, live log lines per cell, cancel button, footer chip reading run folder created.
